2610.13550.title: Personalization Without Stereotyping: Do Speech LLMs Know When to Turn a Deaf Ear?
2610.13550.paper_summary: Recent speech LLMs can leverage rich paralinguistic cues, enabling more complex and personalized interactions. However, little work investigates how this sensitivity can lead to stereotyping, and existing evaluations largely measure demographic disparities without distinguishing beneficial personalization from stereotypical behavior. We introduce BASIS-Bench, a benchmark designed to disentangle these two aspects through three axes: (1) demographic robustness, measuring disparities in content-based tasks across speakers and demographic classification capabilities; (2) stereotypical bias, measuring whether perceived demographic cues trigger unprompted stereotypical behavior; and (3) personalization, measuring whether models can tailor responses to demographic characteristics when explicitly requested. We evaluate eight recent speech LLMs and find that, despite often recognizing demographic cues, most fail to translate them into appropriate personalization. Explicit demographic labels improve personalization but also amplify stereotypical associations already present in the textual backbones. These findings highlight the need to train speech LLMs not only to perceive demographic cues, but to learn when they should shape their responses.
2610.13550.paper_summary_zh: 最近的語音 LLM 可以利用豐富的副語言線索，實現更複雜和個性化的互動。<lb/>然而，對於這種敏感性如何導致刻板印象的研究相對較少，現有的評估主要測量人口統計差異，而未能區分有益的個性化與刻板行為。<lb/>我們引入了 BASIS-Bench，一個旨在通過三個軸心來解開這兩個方面的基準： (1) 人口統計穩健性，測量不同說話者在基於內容的任務中的差異以及人口統計分類能力； (2) 刻板偏見，測量感知的人口統計線索是否會觸發自發的刻板行為；以及 (3) 個性化，測量模型在明確要求時是否能根據人口特徵調整回應。<lb/>我們評估了八個最近的語音 LLM，發現儘管它們通常能識別人口統計線索，但大多數未能將其轉化為適當的個性化。<lb/>明確的人口標籤改善了個性化，但也放大了文本基礎中已存在的刻板聯想。<lb/>這些發現突顯了訓練語音 LLM 的必要性，不僅要能夠感知人口統計線索，還要學會在何時應該調整其回應。
